assessments.reasoning: GNU’s 1.3 publisher file at [19211,20299) contains the full version-choice section. Its final sentence ties permanent permission to designation by the Document and public acceptance by that proxy. The preceding alternatives explain how the same version could independently be available even if the proxy conditions fail.

challenge.method: Place an operative designation elsewhere in the Document’s authorized terms, remove it entirely, and vary the designated proxy’s communication between private and public. Test a separate numbered or-later grant when the proxy route fails.
challenge.results: A designation in an authorized appendix suffices if it grants the relevant authority. With public acceptance, the accepted version becomes a permanent option. Without designation, a volunteer’s public announcement supplies no proxy authority. A designated proxy’s private acceptance alone also fails. An independent or-later grant still permits the specified edition or a later non-draft edition published by the FSF. Section 10 separately allows any FSF-published non-draft edition when the Document specifies no version number.

limitations: A particular work’s authorized terms establish the proxy’s identity and authority. The generic license document, its illustrative Addendum and a catalog label cannot by themselves establish that grant.
The proxy’s public statement and the version it accepts would require evidence in a work-specific inquiry.
reasoning: GNU FDL 1.3 §10 makes the accepted version a permanent option for the Document when its authorized terms empower a proxy to decide which future versions may be used and that proxy publicly accepts the version. The licensee retains the choice. The clause specifies no required location within the Document for the operative designation.
